title: Year 8 retrieval quiz on the year's texts
subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Writing to argue and persuade; end of year
source: Seeded from english/y8 lesson 67 (Year 8 retrieval quiz on the year's texts (portal))
intro: Covers lessons 67 to 82 of Writing to argue and persuade; end of year. Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: What links Squealer and Mark Antony?
options: both use persuasive language to move a crowd
questions.a: A) both use persuasive language to move a crowd. Both are skilled persuaders who change how a crowd thinks.

questions.q: Q5 is worth 12 marks. What must you do?
options: give your view and support it with evidence from the text
questions.a: B) give your view and support it with evidence from the text. An evaluation question needs a judgement backed by evidence.

questions.q: Which plan is strongest for Task A?
options: Clear view; three PEEDL points; a counter-argument; conclusion
questions.a: C) Clear view; three PEEDL points; a counter-argument; conclusion. A plan with a position, points and a counter-argument gives the article structure.

questions.q: What is the speaker's position?
questions.a: A) the greatest leaders serve. The final sentence states the position clearly.

questions.q: Which is the most arguable position?
options: Pupils should elect their class leaders every term.
questions.a: B) Pupils should elect their class leaders every term.. An arguable position is one people could disagree with.

questions.q: Which sentence DEVELOPS the point 'Elections are fairer'?
options: Over time, this builds trust in the leaders.
questions.a: C) Over time, this builds trust in the leaders.. Develop pushes the idea further, here to a long-term consequence.

questions.q: When is a rhetorical method most effective?
options: when it strengthens a clear point
when it hides a weak argument
questions.a: A) when it strengthens a clear point. Methods should serve the argument; overuse weakens it.

questions.q: Which opening best starts the third point?
questions.a: B) Crucially, elections help us grow.. 'Crucially' signals the most important point and links to the argument.

questions.q: Which refutation is strongest?
options: I do not care what they think.
Clear criteria reward responsibility, not popularity.
questions.a: C) Clear criteria reward responsibility, not popularity.. It answers the objection with a reason; the others dismiss it.

questions.q: What weakens a conclusion?
questions.a: A) introducing a brand-new point. A new point at the end confuses the audience; the others draw the argument together.

questions.q: Which redraft is strongest?
options: Voices are important for pupils and stuff.
Every pupil deserves a voice in who leads them.
Pupils should maybe have some voice.
questions.a: B) Every pupil deserves a voice in who leads them.. It is direct, precise and confident.

questions.q: Someone asks, 'What if the elected leader is unfair?' Best response?
options: That's a fair concern; that is why leaders should be accountable and can be replaced.
questions.a: C) That's a fair concern; that is why leaders should be accountable and can be replaced.. Acknowledging the concern and answering with a reason shows confidence and fairness.

questions.q: What most improves an evaluation answer?
questions.a: A) weighing evidence before a judgement. Evaluation needs evidence weighed to reach a judgement.

questions.q: Which redraft best improves 'The street was busy and loud.'?
options: The street was busy, loud and big.
Buses sighed at the kerb and a stall hissed and spat.
The street was very, very busy.
questions.a: B) Buses sighed at the kerb and a stall hissed and spat.. Precise verbs and personification show busyness instead of telling it.

questions.q: Which skill helps most in every unit?
options: analysing a writer's choices with evidence
questions.a: C) analysing a writer's choices with evidence. Analysis with evidence is the thread through every text.

questions.q: Which summer plan is most realistic?
options: 20 minutes a day, after Fajr or before bed
Read ten books in the last week
Read when I feel like it
questions.a: A) 20 minutes a day, after Fajr or before bed. A small, regular habit works better than a last-minute rush.

questions.q: Who leads the pigs in Animal Farm after the Rebellion?
questions.a: B) Napoleon

questions.q: Who says 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears'?
questions.a: B) Mark Antony

questions.q: Which poem is by John Agard?
questions.a: B) Checking Out Me History

questions.q: In the test, reading and writing are worth...
questions.a: C) the same marks
